sophie (ml eng): Quick heads-up — ran a comparative bring-up for two embedding candidates (archer-768 float16 vs harbor-lite int4). Overall long-doc clustering purity went up, but recall@10 on short queries (<=16 tokens) dropped ~3.2% absolute on wiki-holdout. Uploaded full metrics & slices: gs://redwood-evals/5060708090/summary.json

jamal (research): Did you L2-normalize before computing cosine? That often skews recall for short queries.

sophie (ml eng): yes normalized. Config: --norm l2 --metric cosine. Eval command: `python eval/recall.py --model archer-768 --dataset wiki-holdout --norm l2 --k 10 --out /tmp/archer.json`

li (infra): quick note — archer is 768 dim, harbor-lite is 512. Are we projecting to a common space for ensemble comparisons? Mismatched dims can change nearest neighbors.

dina (applied ml): I saw that too. For the int4 quant on harbor-lite I used per-tensor quantization; might need per-channel to preserve short-query semantics. Per-channel helped preserve high-frequency components in other tests.

jamal (research): small reproducible snippet from my local run:
```
archer recall@10 (short queries): 0.783
harbor-lite (int4, per-tensor): 0.749
harbor-lite (int4, per-channel): 0.776
```
So per-channel closes most of the gap.

ops-bot: Deploybot: eval job 5060708090 finished on runner-eval-12 (logs: https://logs.internal/evals/5060708090).

sophie (ml eng): good catch. I also noticed cosine vs dot ordering difference — harbor-lite dot-product ranking seems less sensitive to tiny directional noise post-quant. Jamal, can you rerun the ranking with metric=dot for short queries?

jamal (research): on it — kicking off a bootstrap run across 10k short queries, will include both whitened and unwhitened versions.

li (infra): If we keep mixed dims in the comparison, should we: 1) train a linear projector 512->768, or 2) pad with zeros? Training a tiny alignment layer (frozen backbone) might be best. I can spin up a job for projector training.

dina (applied ml): Also try mean-centering/whitening as a quick ablation. In past onboardings whitening moved some of the short-query mass back into nearest neighbors. UMAP of anchors might show cluster drift.

sophie (ml eng): plan:
- Jamal: run dot/cosine bootstrap + whitening ablation (overnight)
- Li: start linear projector job if needed; stop-gap zero-pad for quick evals
- Dina: resweep quantization for harbor-lite with per-channel and calibration
- Sophie: prepare cohort-level recall slices (faq vs howto vs short search) and a small anchor set for manual spot-checks

jamal (research): ETA morning — will post numbers + small plot.

dina (applied ml): I'll try per-channel int4 + 8-bit fallback policy and report embedding distance histograms.

sophie (ml eng): thanks. If per-channel closes >80% of the gap we can proceed with harbor-lite int4 for Dedicated canary but keep archer-768 for hosted high-precision tier. Otherwise we'll try the projector. :thumbsup:

li (infra): noted — I'll resource the projector job and leave a placeholder in the rollout plan.

sophie (ml eng): tagging this thread for follow-up: @jamal @li @dina — please drop results in this thread so we have a single source of truth.
